problem: Uncertainty quantification for large language models relies on computationally expensive repeated sampling, making practical application difficult with limited samples.
approach: Proposes a modified semantic alphabet size estimator that adjusts discrete semantic entropy for sample coverage to improve uncertainty estimation accuracy.
contribution: Provides more accurate semantic entropy estimation from few samples with high interpretability, flagging incorrect LLM responses effectively.

problem: Existing molecular conformer generation methods overlook the hierarchical structural organization of molecules, producing poor-quality conformers.
approach: Develops a multi-scale generation framework that starts from coarse-grained scaffolds and progressively refines using structural guidance with molecular upsampling to bridge scale gaps.
contribution: Generates more stable and chemically plausible molecular conformers that integrate seamlessly with existing generative models.

problem: Objective assessment of audio source separation still mismatches subjective human perception, especially when interference and distortion interact.
approach: Introduces perceptual measures that isolate leakage and distortion factors by generating reference distortions, encoding them with self-supervised models, and embedding via diffusion maps.
contribution: Provides differentiable, high-resolution measures that rank first or second against 14 widely-used metrics in correlation with subjective human judgment.

problem: Fixed time-frequency resolution trade-offs in classical transforms limit speech emotion recognition by failing to capture informative spectro-temporal structure.
approach: Formulates learnable fractional-order superlet transforms with end-to-end optimization of frequency grids, base cycles, and fractional weights, combined with a sparse denoising module.
contribution: Introduces a fully differentiable front-end that achieves improved speech emotion recognition through learned spectro-temporal analysis.

problem: Online learning in Stackelberg games with side information achieves suboptimal O(T^{2/3}) regret under bandit feedback.
approach: Reduces the problem to linear contextual bandits in utility space, using a linear bandit algorithm to recommend utilities that are inverted to determine mixed strategies.
contribution: Achieves O(T^{1/2}) regret under bandit feedback, an improvement over previously known rates, with empirical outperformance on numerical simulations.

problem: Direct encoding for spiking neural networks proves less robust than rate encoding due to elevated gradient temporal collinearity undermining adversarial robustness.
approach: Introduces gradient temporal collinearity as a measure of directional gradient alignment across time, then proposes structured temporal orthogonal decorrelation using parametric orthogonal kernels.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on visual classification benchmarks in robustness while maintaining representational capacity.

problem: Autoregressive language models are serial and slow; standard discrete diffusion requires hundreds to thousands of evaluations, trading serial depth for iterative breadth.
approach: Proposes FS-DFM, a discrete flow-matching model that makes sampling steps an explicit parameter, paired with reliable update rules and strong teacher guidance from long-run trajectories.
contribution: Achieves 1024-token generation with 8 sampling steps at perplexity parity to 1024-step baselines, delivering 128× faster sampling.

problem: Extending multilingual safety alignment to other languages requires substantial resources, limiting scalability across linguistic communities.
approach: Proposes a plug-and-play Multi-Lingual Consistency loss that improves collinearity between multilingual representation vectors to enforce directional consistency at the semantic level.
contribution: Enhances multilingual safety alignment with limited supervision and improved cross-lingual generalization while maintaining general model utility.

problem: Graph anomaly detection across diverse domains is hindered by different feature semantics and dimensions, and lacks foundational models for zero-shot cross-domain detection.
approach: Proposes OWLEYE, which aligns cross-domain features while preserving domain-specific semantics, learns shared structural patterns via dictionary learning, and enables in-context learning.
contribution: Enables zero-shot graph anomaly detection across unseen domains without retraining, with continuous and scaling-up learning capabilities.

problem: Understanding reasoning strategies in chain-of-thought remains limited; predefined strategy categories fail to capture full diversity of model behaviors.
approach: Automatically extracts diverse reasoning criteria from model-generated CoTs, clusters them into representative categories, and derives contrastive rubrics for interpretation.
contribution: Produces more interpretable analyses, enables prediction of model reasoning strategy, and improves problem-solving and safety benchmarks.

problem: Decision-focused learning relies on deterministic point predictions, which are insufficient to capture intrinsic stochasticity of real-world environments.
approach: Proposes diffusion-based DFL that trains a diffusion model to represent parameter distributions and optimizes decisions by solving stochastic optimization with diffusion samples.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines in decision quality through end-to-end training with a lightweight score function estimator.

problem: Collaboration mechanisms in VAE-based collaborative filtering remain underexplored; binary input masking improves performance but lacks theoretical understanding.
approach: Analyzes collaboration via latent proximity, derives a sharing radius governing when updates reduce loss on other users, and proposes an anchor regularizer to enable global consistency.
contribution: Characterizes trade-offs between local and global collaboration, enabling better mixing while preserving user identity.

problem: Existing flowchart datasets lack fine-grained control over structural properties and rendering styles, limiting training of multimodal LLMs on visual reasoning tasks.
approach: Introduces FlowGen, a controllable synthesizer that generates flowcharts with customizable structural features and multiple renderer backends for systematic evaluation.
contribution: Training on FlowGen substantially improves flowchart parsing and QA, while exposing MLLM weaknesses in handling structural complexity and rendering diversity.

problem: Self-improvement in math reasoning is believed exclusive to RL approaches due to SL's reliance on reference answers and inability to reflect on mistakes.
approach: Proposes Negative-aware Fine-Tuning, which constructs an implicit negative policy from self-generated incorrect answers to enable reflection and improvement.
contribution: Matches or surpasses leading RL algorithms like GRPO and DAPO on math reasoning while showing SL and RL equivalence in strict on-policy training.

problem: Policy optimization methods for LLM reasoning with verifiable rewards suffer from training instability and diversity collapse.
approach: Formalizes math reasoning as a finite-horizon MDP and proves optimal actions can be recovered from Q-functions of a fixed random policy, bypassing policy iteration.
contribution: ROVER translates this insight into a minimalist yet highly effective RL algorithm that samples actions from softmax over uniform-policy Q-values.

problem: Expert merging for Mixture-of-Experts compression introduces irreducible error by losing fine-grained routing control, especially for generative tasks.
approach: Proposes Router-weighted Expert Activation Pruning that considers both router gate-values and expert activation norms to minimize reconstruction error.
contribution: Consistently outperforms merging methods on generative benchmarks at 50% compression, achieving near-lossless compression on code generation tasks.

problem: Theoretical foundations underlying transformer success remain largely unexplored, particularly their learning capabilities across diverse scenarios.
approach: Theoretically analyzes transformers as students learning from teacher models including convolutions, graph layers, and statistical models via simplified position-only attention.
contribution: Proves one-layer transformers with simplified attention can recover all parameter blocks of teacher models and generalize well to out-of-distribution data.

problem: Achieving differential privacy on Hadamard manifolds is computationally intensive, requiring MCMC sampling for practical implementation.
approach: Proposes Exponential-Wrapped Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms that operate entirely within manifold intrinsic geometry without MCMC sampling.
contribution: Achieves multiple DP notions on general Hadamard manifolds with superior utility and runtime on synthetic and real-world data.

problem: Traditional critics learn absolute state values despite only value differences being relevant for decision-making, wasting capacity.
approach: Proposes Relative Value Learning that learns antisymmetric value differences directly via a pairwise Bellman operator with well-posed targets.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on Atari benchmarks compared to standard PPO, demonstrating relative value estimation as an effective alternative.

problem: Post-training in language models can reduce in-context steerability and output space coverage, limiting performance on multi-answer tasks.
approach: Introduces Spectrum Suite with >40 data sources spanning >90 tasks requiring steering to diverse distributions, and proposes Spectrum Tuning for improved steerability.
contribution: Improves over pretrained and instruction-tuned models in steerability, distributional coverage, and alignment on held-out datasets.

problem: Existing MCP benchmarks are narrow, focus on read-heavy tasks, and fail to capture complexity of real-world agent workflows.
approach: Proposes MCPMark with 127 high-quality tasks involving diverse CRUD operations, curated initial states, and programmatic verification scripts.
contribution: Best models reach only 52.56% pass@1 on MCPMark, exposing significant weaknesses in current LLMs despite high performance on simpler benchmarks.

problem: Self-supervised learning for inverse problems struggles with single incomplete observation models, lacking ground truth for training.
approach: Proposes equivariant splitting that combines self-supervised splitting losses with equivariant reconstruction networks to produce unbiased estimates.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on image inpainting, accelerated MRI, sparse-view CT, and compressive sensing with highly rank-deficient models.

problem: Rate-distortion theory lacks practical algorithmic approaches for computing the tradeoff between rate and reconstruction error.
approach: Exploits connection to entropic optimal transport via stochastic control, using Schrodinger's result to solve a backward heat equation for optimal reconstruction.
contribution: Provides novel diffusion-based numerical method for estimating rate-distortion functions with demonstrated effectiveness on multiple examples.

problem: Modeling 4D hand motion is fragmented into separate estimation and generation tasks, missing knowledge transfer opportunities and limiting condition flexibility.
approach: Proposes UniHand, a unified diffusion framework that treats both estimation and generation as conditional motion synthesis with joint VAE for heterogeneous condition alignment.
contribution: Delivers robust hand motion modeling maintaining performance under severe occlusions and temporally incomplete inputs.

problem: Learning Fourier-sparse Boolean functions requires prior knowledge of sparsity parameter; existing testers have high query complexity.
approach: Designs a new tester with query complexity O(s^4) independent of ambient dimension and proves lower bound of Omega(s).
contribution: Improves upon best known results with significantly reduced query complexity and matching lower bounds for Fourier sparsity testing.

problem: Data selection for instruction tuning faces challenge of identifying high-quality subsets from large datasets to unlock specific or general LLM capabilities.
approach: Proposes Nait, which evaluates data impact by analyzing neuron activation pattern similarity between IT dataset and target domain capabilities.
contribution: Training on 10% selected Alpaca-GPT4 subset consistently outperforms methods using external models or uncertainty features across various tasks.

problem: Mamba-based multimodal LLMs have redundant visual tokens inflating inference cost, with prefill stage dominating total latency.
approach: Proposes DTP with two-level microscaling for sensitive activations and automatic weight scaling that derives importance from Mamba's internal parameters.
contribution: Reduces computation by nearly 50%, maintains higher performance than existing pruning methods, and achieves over 35% prefill latency reduction.

problem: Learning effectively from autonomous data in batch online RL is challenging; existing methods often fail to improve efficiently.
approach: Systematically studies three axes: algorithm class, policy extraction methods, and policy expressivity; finds Q-functions significantly improve performance over imitation-based methods.
contribution: Shows implicit policy extraction via best action in distribution outperforms explicit methods, and expressive policy classes are necessary for scaling.

problem: Finding correct initialization for transformers is crucial but lacks asymptotically exact prescriptions; wrong initialization causes rank or entropy collapse.
approach: Provides analytical theory of signal propagation through deep transformers with exact treatment of self-attention via parallel with Random Energy Model.
contribution: Yields simple algorithm to compute trainability diagrams identifying correct initialization hyper-parameters while analyzing gradient vanishing.

problem: Safe and feasible trajectory planning requires safety awareness, but expert demonstrations often lack explicit safety principles and inherit human driving errors.
approach: Proposes Plan-R1 with two-stage approach: pre-train on expert data then fine-tune with GRPO using rule-based rewards; introduces Variance-Decoupled GRPO to preserve safety-critical objectives.
contribution: Aligns planning with safety principles while discarding undesirable patterns, maintaining human-like behaviors on nuPlan benchmark.

problem: FP8 training of large language models poses challenges for numerical stability due to reduced precision; current frameworks have efficiency overhead.
approach: Proposes MOSS with two-level microscaling strategy for activations and automatic scaling for weights that predicts factors during training.
contribution: Enables efficient FP8 training of 7B models achieving performance comparable to BF16 baseline with up to 34% higher training throughput.

problem: Understanding which parts of chain-of-thought actually contribute to correct answers remains unclear; hidden patterns underlie reasoning success.
approach: Introduces potential metric quantifying contribution of each CoT part to answer likelihood; analyzes patterns including non-monotonicity, spikes, and lucky guesses.
contribution: Identifies surprising reasoning patterns and measures CoT transferability across models, revealing key insights about reasoning mechanisms.

problem: Predicting diverse future human trajectories requires handling stochasticity, but existing diffusion methods enforce skeleton consistency indirectly.
approach: Proposes KinemaDiff with Joint-Adaptive Noise Generator for heterogeneous per-joint noise and Structure-Aligned Constraint Enforcer encoding skeletal topology.
contribution: Enables direct control over physical realism and motion diversity while guaranteeing anatomical consistency.

problem: Vision-language models have limited fine-grained visual perception, a critical bottleneck for real-world applications due to scarcity of high-quality data.
approach: Proposes ViPER, a self-bootstrapping framework using coarse-to-fine learning with image and instance-level reconstruction plus two-stage reinforcement learning.
contribution: Achieves average 1.7% gain on seven benchmarks with up to 6.0% improvement on fine-grained perception while maintaining generalizability.

problem: Computer vision tasks share substantial overlapping information, but conventional codecs ignore this, leading to redundant representations.
approach: Develops learnable three-channel codec inspired by Gray-Wyner network to disentangle common and task-specific information via lossy common information.
contribution: Substantially reduces redundancy and consistently outperforms independent coding across multiple vision task scenarios.

problem: Language models default to narrow high-probability outputs, causing homogeneous generation and mode collapse across runs.
approach: Proposes STARS, which optimizes steering directions on Stiefel manifold at each token to maximize geometric volume of steered activations across concurrent runs.
contribution: Consistently outperforms standard sampling on test generation and discovery benchmarks with greater diversity without sacrificing performance.

problem: Current motion-conditioned video generation suffers from prohibitive latency preventing real-time interaction.
approach: Presents MotionStream with self-forcing distillation and sliding-window causal attention with attention sinks to enable streaming generation.
contribution: Achieves sub-second latency with up to 29 FPS streaming generation on single GPU, enabling infinite-length streaming with state-of-the-art quality.

problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning initializes low-rank adaptation with only leading singular vectors, confining representation capacity to a narrow subspace.
approach: Proposes SumRA that initializes each row of adaptation matrix as sum of multiple singular vectors beyond leading components.
contribution: Improves word error rate on multilingual ASR from 14.42% to 12.41% over LoRA with 50% fewer trainable parameters.

problem: Existing LLM interpretability methods overlook nonlinear, relational geometry of representation spaces; adversarial effects on latent spaces remain poorly understood.
approach: Applies persistent homology to measure representation space geometry under adversarial influence, uncovering topological signature of adversarial effects.
contribution: Reveals consistent topological compression across architectures where latent spaces collapse from varied features into fewer dominant ones.

problem: Most material property prediction readouts assume atom-decomposability, a strong bias that limits application to spatial properties like gas adsorption.
approach: Proposes SpatialRead with region-based decomposition using voxelized space and spatial nodes, transforming atomic graphs into heterogeneous atom-space graphs.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art pre-trained foundation models on spatial property tasks while highlighting importance of physically grounded readout design.
